sentences.text: Saichania was a medium-sized, herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Mongolia and China during the Late Cretaceous.
This animal measured between 5 and 7 meters in length and weighed between 1.4 and 2.0 metric tons.
It had a flat, low body supported by four short legs.
The holotype skull of Saichania is broad, measuring 455 millimeters in length and 480 millimeters in width.
The atlas and axis vertebrae of Saichania are fused together.
Its neck was protected by two rings of six rectangular osteoderms each.
Saichania's tail ended in a bulbous club that may have been highly vascularized to mimic a false head and confuse predators.
A 1998 CT scan study by William Gallagher revealed that specimen PIN 3142/250 had a healed puncture wound from a tyrannosaur tooth above its right eye socket.
The first fossils of Saichania were discovered in the early 1970s within the Baruungoyot Formation by a Polish-Mongolian expedition.
This expedition found the remains in the Gobi Desert near Chulsan in 1970 and 1971.
The type species Saichania chulsanensis was formally named in 1977.
The genus name Saichania comes from the Mongolian word for 'beautiful', referencing the excellent preservation of the type specimen.
Saichania used a tail club to defend itself against predators such as Tarbosaurus.
Saichania used a horny beak to bite off plants in its desert habitat and processed them in a wide hindgut.
Saichania's skull contained very complex air passages, including a scroll-like turbinate bone structure that likely helped condense and preserve exhaled moisture.
Researchers suggest Saichania's complex air passages may have allowed it to cool inhaled air and limit water loss.
Saichania's unusually strongly ossified hard palate likely allowed it to eat tough plants.
The anatomical features of Saichania suggest it lived in a hot, arid environment.
Some evidence suggests Saichania may have possessed a salt gland near its nostrils to aid survival in a desert habitat.
Researchers suggested that the relative abundance of ankylosaur species in the area was caused by them being the main herbivores, providing enough food for three populations.
Maryańska classified Saichania as a member of the Ankylosauridae family, noting its unique nasal cavity structure.
Tianzhenosaurus and Shanxia have been proposed as potential synonyms of Saichania.
Later cladistic analyses recovered a position for Saichania in Ankylosaurinae, often near Tarchia.
Saichania belongs to the parent group Ankylosaurinae.
Saichania lived during the Late Cretaceous period between 75 and 70 million years ago in what is now Asia.
Saichania lived from the Cenomanian to the Campanian stages, between 100.5 and 72.2 million years ago.
Saichania is more closely related to Asian ankylosaurs like Pinacosaurus and Tarchia than to North American ones like Ankylosaurus.

In 2014, Victoria Megan Arbour debated that a previously described juvenile specimen was misleadingly reconstructed with a skull cast from the holotype and likely belonged to a different ankylosaur, possibly Pinacosaurus.
The referral of specimen PIN 3142/250 to Saichania was contested by Penkalski and Tumanova, who argued it belonged to a new species of Tarchia, T. teresae.
The theory that Saichania's tail club mimicked a false head is less scientifically accepted than the traditional weapon hypothesis.
